items.title: Nobody wants your AI app
items.summary_original: The switchboard operator’s job was automated out of existence. The work it became, the invisible systems that now connect every call, is worth more than the job ever was. AI is about to do the same thing to the app. The people buying AI are blunt about the fact that the future is intelligence that disappears into existing platforms. Everyone wants it invisible and under their total control at the same time. We are all racing to build AI apps that nobody wants to open. items.title: UFO-shaped futuro house brings radical 1960s vision of prefab living to the market
items.summary_original: UFO-shaped residence in california hits the market for $1.5 million A UFO-shaped Futuro house in Idyllwild, California , is on the market for $1.495 million. Designed by Finnish architect Matti Suuronen, the prefabricated dwelling was conceived as a portable ski cabin that could be transported by helicopter and installed in remote locations. With fewer than 100 Futuros built, the property offers a rare surviving example of a Space Age experiment in portable living. Its elliptical yellow fiberglass shell, circular windows and aircraft-style entrance reflect a period when space exploration and advances in synthetic materials fascinated designers, leading them to imagine radically different ways of living. all images courtesy of Sotheby's International Realty the Matti Suuronen-designed house

items.summary_original: By day she advises international law firms. By night, the antique-mould collector shapes crowns, castles and sea serpents out of jelly. There was a time when your jelly said more about you than your wallpaper. The Victorians were the first to work out how to clarify it, colour it and add flavour to it, and once they had, a wobbling tower of it on the dinner table meant you'd made it. items.title: Stop Treating CSS Container Queries Like Traditional Media Queries
items.summary_original: To be completely honest with you, I missed the news when CSS Container Queries first shipped. And when I finally heard about it, my very first thought was, “Why exactly do I need this when media queries already exist?” I’m not proud of that reaction, knowing what I know now, but it was comforting to know that I wasn’t alone. In fact, there are legions of us out there. What baffles me is that container queries aren’t a new feature, as it currently sits at around 94% browser support . And yet, very few people are actually using it. According to the State of CSS survey, 86% of developers are aware of container queries, but only 41.4% actually use them. Surveys can be biased and not completely representative of our entire field, but this one is certainly the best indicator we’ve got. Kevin Pow

French photographer and videographer Alix Urien believes the answer may lie in the way we look rather than in what we see. In her series Circa 2020s, created between Paris and Normandy, she transforms ordinary contemporary scenes into photographs and videos shaped by the light, color and fleeting sensations of nineteenth-century Impressionism. items.summary_de: IM ZEITGENÖSSISCHEN PARIS DEN Impressionismus FINDEN Existiert das Paris der großen impressionistischen Maler noch? Die französische Fotografin und Videofilmerin Alix Urien glaubt, dass die Antwort eher in der Art und Weise liegt, wie wir aussehen, als in dem, was wir sehen. In ihrer zwischen Paris und der Normandie entstandenen Serie Circa 2020s verwandelt sie gewöhnliche zeitgenössische Szenen in Fotografien und Videos, die vom Licht, der Farbe und den flüchtigen Empfindungen des Impressionismus des 19. Jahrhunderts geprägt sind. Anstatt berühmte Gemälde durch die Kameralinse zu reproduzieren, erforscht Urien die Emotionen, die verschiedene Generationen verbinden, und legt nahe, dass sich Städte und Gesellschaften zwar weiterentwickeln, bestimmte menschliche Erfahrungen jedoch bemerkenswert unverändert bleiben. „Der Impressionismus war eine Antwort auf eine sich verändernde Welt“, erzählt Urien designboom und erinnert sich an die Industrialisierung

We've all got a place that's dear to our heart, that we visited years ago, and which we have a clear picture of in our mind. It might be a country lane, a riverbank or simply a view from a train window. You're convinced you can remember it like yesterday. And yet if you ever revisit it, years later, you're often surprised by how different it looks in reality. Memory is, let's face it, not a reliable tool. Visual details in our minds blur, shift and get mixed together gradually, over time. It's not a big problem – it's just the way the brain works. When you analyse it logically, there's nothing in our nearest astronomical neighbour that looks remotely like a face. But our brains are wired to see faces in everything, from a power socket to the front grille of a car to a house with two windows and a door. items.title: Recap: ADC Design Conference 2026
items.summary_original: On October 5, the Haus der Wirtschaft in Stuttgart became a meeting point for designers, creatives, and people interested in design. For one day, the ADC Design Conference 2026 placed the practice of design at the center of attention. Under the guiding theme “Change the World with Design,” the conference explored typography, branding, motion design, visual systems, spaces, and architecture, but above all, it asked what good design means today. Around 600 visitors and 40 speakers came together across two stages to discuss current developments as well as fundamental questions surrounding design practice. While the Creative Stage focused on concrete projects, creative processes, and personal perspectives, the Business Stage looked more closely at the economic and social significance of design

items.title: A Practical Guide To Naming Things
items.summary_original: Naming is hard. The language we use shapes the way we think about things, but also the conversation we have about it. That’s why we have so much confusion about colors, icons, UI components, features — and that’s why we struggle to name design tokens, HTML classes, and variables. Sometimes, the names we choose are too generic , so it’s difficult to understand what exactly is meant. And sometimes they are too specific , leaving little room for flexibility and reuse. How do we choose the right names? And which naming conventions work best? Let’s take a closer look. How To Name Things If you’re looking for some inspiration for naming HTML classes, CSS properties, or JavaScript functions, Classnames is a wonderful resource jam-packed with ideas that get you thinking outside the box . items.summary_de: vor dem ersten Foto Manchmal komme ich an ein Gebäude und mache in der ersten Stunde kein Foto. Ich laufe herum. Ich betrachte das Licht, den Boden, die Decke, die Art und Weise, wie ein Raum in einen anderen übergeht. Ich achte auf die Materialien und darauf, wie sie sich je nach Standpunkt verändern. Manchmal kenne ich das Gebäude gut von Fotos. Manchmal bin ich weit gereist, um einen Ort zu sehen, auf den ich schon seit Jahren neugierig bin. Manchmal komme ich an und habe kaum eine Vorstellung davon, was mich erwarten wird. Normalerweise habe ich eine Vorstellung davon, wonach ich suche. Es ist ziemlich oft falsch. Sobald ich tatsächlich dort bin, fühlt sich das Gebäude anders an. Ein Foto kann einem einen Eindruck von einem Ort vermitteln, aber es kann einem nie wirklich sagen, wie es sich anfühlt, darin zu stehen. Du weißt nicht, wie die Schatten fallen, wie das Licht

Created by ACCIONA Cultura in exclusive collaboration with Madrid’s Museo Nacional del Prado, the 30-minute free-roam virtual reality installation invites visitors to step inside the canvas and explore classic art together. Driven by academic curatorship and faithful replication, the experience combines original storytelling, meticulous spatial design, and immersive soundscapes, turning passive viewing into an intimate, shared sensory journey. items.title: Foundry Kingdom
items.summary_original: Foundry Kingdom is not champagne—it is a pint of bitter in the local pub. It is not the King’s horse at Ascot, but the drayman’s horse hauling beer barrels through narrow streets. It is not spectacle or ceremony, but industrial labour: the quiet dignity of work. Rooted in the early English grotesques of the 19th century, Foundry Kingdom carries an industrial echo of cast metal, railway lettering, and newspaper type battered by use. But it avoids nostalgia for its own sake. Instead, it feels contemporary in its restraint, as though those historical references have been absorbed and reinterpreted rather than imitated. It carries the spirit of a nation shaped not by rulers, but by its people—those who built, dug, carried and endured. Grotesques emerged from the smog of the early English Indus

items.title: tree-mounted machines connect to web app to let users knock on wood remotely
items.summary_original: web app turns superstition into remote-controlled device Knock On Wood is an internet-connected device that performs the familiar gesture of knocking on wood , allowing users to follow the superstition remotely when no wood is nearby. Through a web app , users press a digital button to trigger a physical device that knocks on wood in real time. The project is part of an ongoing series, Machines Responding to Superstitions, by designers Shashwath Santosh and Nithin Eluvathingal. Drawing on industrial design, engineering, manufacturing, critical thought, and world-building, the series uses machines to examine everyday beliefs and rituals. It was actually back in 2012 that he created his first documentary on the Swiss architect, Notes from a Day in the Life of an Architect, which was a shorter film that ignited this more-than-decade-long exploration of his portfolio. items.title: Sind das etwa …? Nein, sind es nicht!
items.summary_original: Den inszenierten Skandal dahinter hätte es gar nicht gebraucht, denn die augenzwinkernde Kampagne, mit der die antibakteriellen Feuchtücher Wet Ones daran erinnern, für was sie gedacht sind, ist auch so ein schöner Spaß. Gerade auch in Zeiten von KI. Zum Start der Kampagne, die die Agentur Bartle Bogle Hegarty USA (BBH) für die antibakteriellen Feuchttücher Wet Ones entwickelt hat, sah man den (vermeintlich) nackten Pop von Kyle Cooke, Star der Bravo-Serie »Summer House«. Doch natürlich hat er nicht wirklich blank gezogen. Denn der Dreh, der hinter der Kampagne steht, ist viel schöner. Und auch smarter. Denn sie reagiert auf eine Kund:innen-Umfrage , in der ans Licht kam, dass manche User:innen die feuchten Hand-Tücher, die auch wirklich nur für die Hände gedacht sind, auch nach dem Toilet

items.title: stefan sagmeister and ekn transform global data into colorful sneakers and boots
items.summary_original: STEFAN SAGMEISTER AND EKN TURN DATA INTO WEARABLE DESIGN Stefan Sagmeister is taking his data visualizations somewhere they rarely go: onto people's feet. In collaboration with Frankfurt-based ekn footwear , the Austrian graphic designer has developed a sneaker and a boot that translate statistics on renewable electricity and street homelessness into wearable objects. The two designs accompany his exhibition Finally, Something Good., opening at La Gaîté Lyrique in Paris on October 15, 2026. items.title_de: Stefan Sagmeister und EKN verwandeln globale Daten in farbenfrohe Sneakers und Stiefel
items.summary_de: STEFAN SAGMEISTER UND EKN VERWANDELN DATEN IN WEARABLE DESIGN Stefan Sagmeister bringt seine Datenvisualisierungen dorthin, wo sie selten hinkommen: auf die Füße der Menschen. In Zusammenarbeit mit dem Frankfurter Unternehmen ekn Footwear hat der österreichische Grafikdesigner einen Sneaker und einen Stiefel entwickelt, die Statistiken über erneuerbaren Strom und Obdachlosigkeit auf der Straße in tragbare Objekte übersetzen. Die beiden Entwürfe begleiten seine Ausstellung „Endlich etwas Gutes“, die am 15. Oktober 2026 im La Gaîté Lyrique in Paris eröffnet wird. Anstatt lediglich bestehende Kunstwerke auf Schuhen zu reproduzieren, vereint das Projekt Grafikdesign und traditionelle Schuhmacherei. „Es ging darum zu sehen, was passiert, wenn Stefans Denkweise auf unsere Art, Dinge zu machen, trifft“, erzählt ekn-Gründer Noel Klein-Reesink designboom in einem exklusiven Interview

items.title: solid walnut, oak, and padauk give bathroom flush plates a sculptural identity
items.summary_original: Solid wood gives a functional bathroom detail a sculptural form RTY Studio has developed a collection of solid wood flush plates for Geberit Sigma systems, combining precise geometry with the grain and color variations of American walnut, European oak, and padauk. Designed and crafted in Zagreb, Croatia, by sculptor Tomislav Martinčević, a member of the Croatian Association of Artists (HDLU), the collection reinterprets a functional bathroom detail through material and form. The three models feature clean geometric profiles, crisp upper corners, and rounded lower corners, with two flush buttons integrated into each wooden face. The natural grain and varying tones of the three wood species give each plate a distinct appearance. all images ©RTY Studio CNC machining and hand finishing refine
items.title_de: Massives Walnuss-, Eichen- und Padoukholz verleihen Badezimmer-Betätigungsplatten eine skulpturale Identität
items.summary_de: Massivholz verleiht einem funktionalen Badezimmerdetail eine skulpturale Form. RTY Studio hat eine Kollektion von Betätigungsplatten aus Massivholz für Geberit Sigma-Systeme entwickelt, die präzise Geometrie mit den Maserungs- und Farbvariationen von amerikanischem Nussbaum, europäischer Eiche und Padauk kombinieren. Entworfen und gefertigt in Zagreb, Kroatien, vom Bildhauer Tomislav Martinčević, einem Mitglied des Kroatischen Künstlerverbandes (HDLU), interpretiert die Kollektion ein funktionales Badezimmerdetail durch Material und Form neu. Die drei Modelle zeichnen sich durch klare geometrische Profile, klare obere Ecken und abgerundete untere Ecken aus, wobei in jede Holzoberfläche zwei bündige Tasten integriert sind. Die natürliche Maserung und die unterschiedlichen Farbtöne der drei Holzarten verleihen jeder Platte ein individuelles Aussehen. Alle Bilder ©RTY Studio CNC-Bearbeitung und Handveredelung verfeinern
